description: The bar chart illustrates the number of morphosyntactic probing tasks evaluated for various language families within the context of multilingual BERT models, as presented in the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models.” The vertical axis lists language families or groups, including IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged from top to bottom in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” spans from 0 to 80 in increments of 10, representing the number of probing tasks per language family. The IE-Slavic group has the highest number of tasks, with a bar extending to approximately 79. IE-Romance follows with around 48 tasks, and IE-Germanic has about 44. Uralic is represented by a bar reaching approximately 20 tasks, while IE-Baltic and IE-other are close in value at roughly 18 and 16 tasks, respectively. IE-Indic and Semitic have modest task counts of about 10 and 8, respectively. Turkic and Basque show the lowest counts, with bars reaching approximately 5 and 4 tasks, respectively. Each bar is uniquely colored to distinguish the language families, and the chart uses a horizontal bar format to visually emphasize the comparative magnitude of tasks across groups.
